body:
One comment about the SoftBody3D logic here: this code is somewhat complicated because `SoftBody3D` derives from `MeshInstance3D`, and generally wants to control ownership of the `mesh` property, but it only does so indirectly.

`SoftBody3D` does not directly override or hook into `MeshInstance3D::set_mesh()`, and instead just checks at various points in time later whether or not the `mesh` property has been updated from what it remembers.  Up until recently (#106863) it did this every frame in a `frame_pre_draw` callback.  Now it does it as part of the `NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS` notification, and optionally as part of the the `NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS` notification.

This makes the `SoftBody3D` state rather tricky, and it also means that when running in the editor SoftBody3D often does not detect changes to the `mesh` property, since it doesn't receive `NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS`

How would people feel about having `SoftBody3D` hook into the `MeshInstanc3D::set_mesh()` method somehow, so that it could immediately process changes to the mesh?  We could either make this method virtual and override it, or possibly connect to the `property_list_changed` signal.  I think this would make the `SoftBody3D` logic a bit easier to understand, and less error-prone.

I do think it would be better to fix this by just having `SoftBody3D` process `set_mesh()` call directly, as I discussed above.  The current mesh handling behavior is causing other bugs too (#108059), and having `SoftBody3D` process `set_mesh()` calls directly seems like a simpler fix that will address both of these problems.

I've create #108061 to implement the `set_mesh()` behavior I describe, and I think this PR can be superseded by that one.
